1\. Purpose and design principles
=================================

This document turns the PRD into an implementable design for the engineers who will build UAP and the UPSA staff who will operate it. Each choice states its reason so a later change can be judged on the same grounds.

| **Principle** | **In practice** |
| --- | --- |
| Ledger, not counters | Stock, cost and accounting are append-only records; balances are derived; corrections are new rows. |
| The database enforces the rules | Uniqueness, state transitions, serial and stock rules live in Postgres constraints and functions so no client or script can bypass them. |
| Roles are templates over scopes | Seven role templates map to fine-grained scopes; only the Super Admin holds the administrator flag. |
| Snapshot what was agreed | Prices, tax, exchange rate, BOM version and terms are frozen on the document that used them. |
| Segregation of duties in code | Requesters cannot approve; builders cannot inspect; finance and procurement checks are separate. |
| Idempotent writes | Every mutating endpoint accepts an idempotency key so retries and double clicks are safe. |
| API first | The web app is one client of a versioned API; future clients reuse the same rules. |
| Modular monolith | One deployable API with strict module boundaries; split services only when a measured need appears. |
| Paid where it protects operations | Production tiers for database, backups and monitoring; no cold-start free tiers for anything staff depend on. |

2\. System architecture
=======================

![System architecture](data:image/png;base64,)  
_Figure 1 — Containers and trust boundaries_

*   **One Next.js app for staff.** Server components for fast first load; TanStack Query for interactive tables; role-aware navigation from the user’s scopes. Public and POS apps are not built now, but the monorepo has room for them.
*   **NestJS API (Fastify) with Postgres functions for critical moves.** Goods receipt posting, landed-cost allocation, stock issue, unit finalisation and dispatch run as single database transactions invoked by the API. Invariants are atomic and testable at the database.
*   **Worker on pg-boss.** Jobs share Postgres, enqueue in the same transaction as the business change (transactional outbox) and need no extra service. Redis (Upstash) is used only for rate limits and short caches.
*   **Supabase for Postgres, Auth, Storage and Realtime.** Managed backups with point-in-time recovery, pooling, branching for preview databases, and pgvector for later search. The application tier stays portable because it needs only standard Postgres.
*   **Cloudflare in front.** DNS, TLS, WAF and rate rules; optional Cloudflare Access can gate the app behind UPSA single sign-on as a second layer.

2.1 Three representative flows
------------------------------

1.  **Goods receipt and landed cost:** the Inventory Officer posts a GRN (POST /v1/goods-receipts/{id}/post) which writes ledger rows, lots and component serials and updates quarantine for rejects. Once charges are final, the Procurement Officer runs POST /v1/shipments/{id}/landed-cost/run; the database function allocates charges, writes cost history and queues ledger postings.
2.  **Finishing a unit:** the QC Inspector passes an inspection; prod.finalise\_unit() assigns the final serial, writes component and labour cost snapshots, receives the unit into finished goods, creates the warranty template and queues a label job.
3.  **Dispatch:** the Inventory Officer dispatches reserved units; sales.dispatch\_order() locks the units, writes ledger rows and dispatch note, starts warranty on handover confirmation and queues the invoice and cost-of-sales posting.

====================

| **Layer** | **Recommendation** | **Why** | **Upgrade trigger** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| UI | Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui (Radix), lucide | Accessible primitives you own; tokens map to UPSA brand | — |
| Client data | TanStack Query v5, TanStack Table + Virtual | Caching, optimistic updates, virtualised grids for ledgers | — |
| Forms | React Hook Form + Zod (shared with API) | One schema validates form and API | — |
| API | NestJS 11 on Fastify, OpenAPI generated, typed client via openapi-typescript | Module per domain, guards for scopes, high throughput | Add instances at sustained CPU > 60% or p95 > 300 ms |
| Database | Supabase Pro, Postgres 16+, PITR add-on, Supavisor pooling | Managed recovery, RLS, branching, Realtime, pgvector | Compute Medium → Large; read replica for reports |
| Data access | SQL-first migrations (Supabase CLI) + Drizzle for typed queries | Triggers, partial indexes and RLS are first-class SQL; Drizzle adds types without hiding SQL | — |
| Jobs | pg-boss in apps/worker | Transactional enqueue, retries, schedules, no extra service | Dedicated worker size if queue age > 60 s |
| Cache / limits | Upstash Redis | Serverless sliding-window rate limits | — |
| Auth | Supabase Auth: invite-only, email + TOTP; custom access-token hook adds roles, scopes, is\_admin claims | Claims in the JWT keep RLS checks cheap | SSO via UPSA Google/Microsoft tenant if available |
| Files | Supabase Storage private buckets with signed URLs | Customs documents, photos, QC logs; no public buckets | Cloudflare R2 when > 100 GB |
| Email | Resend with SPF, DKIM and DMARC; provider interface | Reliable transactional email | Second provider for failover |
| PDF and labels | @react-pdf/renderer in worker; Code128/QR labels | Deterministic PO, GRN, invoice, dispatch, warranty and label output | Print agent for silent label printing |
| Search | Postgres full-text + pg\_trgm; pgvector for the later repair KB | Enough for tens of thousands of rows; no extra cluster | Dedicated search only if > 500k records |
| Edge | Cloudflare (Free or Pro) WAF and DNS; optional Access | Shields the origin; second authentication gate | Pro for managed WAF rules |
| Observability | Sentry, OpenTelemetry → Grafana Cloud, Better Stack uptime | Fast detection and traceability | Paid Grafana tier on volume |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions, Vercel previews, Supabase branching, Renovate | Every PR gets a preview app and throwaway database | — |
| Code security | CodeQL, Semgrep, gitleaks, Trivy, dependency review | Catches secrets, injection and vulnerable packages | — |
| Testing | Vitest, Playwright, MSW, pgTAP (RLS, ledger, state machines), k6, axe-core | Rules are tested where they live | — |
| Backups | PITR + nightly encrypted pg\_dump to Cloudflare R2 | Survives a vendor-level incident; quarterly restore drill | — |
| Secrets | Environment groups, Supabase Vault, 1Password | No secrets in the repo | Doppler as the team grows |

3.1 Alternatives considered
---------------------------

| **Option** | **Decision** | **Reason** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ERPNext or Odoo as the base | Not chosen; kept as fallback | Custom fit for imports, genealogy and approvals; ownership and brand |
| Prisma | Rejected | Harder to express partial indexes, RLS and functions; migrations would drift from the database |
| BullMQ + Redis | Rejected for v1 | Extra moving part; pg-boss gives transactional enqueue |
| Microservices | Rejected | Modular monolith is simpler; modules can be extracted later |
| Supabase only (no NestJS) | Rejected | Multi-table transactions and background work are clearer in a service layer; RLS stays as defence in depth |
| Elasticsearch | Deferred | Postgres search meets the scale |
| Firestore / MongoDB | Rejected | Relational integrity and SQL reporting are core to ERP |

4\. Growth path
===============

“Easy to grow” is made concrete: each likely growth direction has a defined step and what is already in place for it.

| **Growth** | **Step** | **Already in place** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| More users or data | Scale Supabase compute; add API instances; read replica for reports; partition ledger and audit monthly (already partitioned) | Pooling, indexes, partitions, report jobs off the primary |
| New client: public storefront, request portal, POS, mobile app | Add apps/<client> to the monorepo; issue API-client credentials with limited scopes; add Turnstile, stricter rate tiers and customer auth | Versioned API, typed client package, scope model, core.api\_clients, idempotency keys, outbox events |
| Offline POS later | Add packages/pos-core (IndexedDB queue, sync endpoint with idempotency, conflict queue) | Idempotency and reservation constraints already protect serial units |
| Online payments later | Implement a PaymentProvider (for example Paystack) and webhook handler | Payments table with provider reference column and verified-webhook pattern in the threat model |
| New domain modules | New Nest module, migration, scope constants and screens | Module boundaries, shared UI package, scope registry |
| UPSA finance or e-invoicing integration | Outbox events → worker → connector; export jobs already exist | Outbox, export, GL postings with idempotent source keys |
| More than one site or company | Add company\_id and site\_id through migration and RLS helper; locations already hierarchical | Location tree, RLS via helper functions |
| Team growth | Module owners, ADRs, CODEOWNERS, contract tests between modules | Monorepo boundaries and typed contracts |
| Extract a service | Extract worker or reporting first (stateless), then a hot module behind the same API | No cross-module table access except through module services |

4.1 Hosting region
------------------

The default is **Frankfurt** for Vercel, Render and Supabase so the tiers sit together; **London** is the alternative. Phase 0 includes a latency measurement from UPSA’s network; the region is fixed after that, since moving a database later is costly. If UPSA requires data on a local server, the standard-Postgres design allows self-hosting at the cost of operating backups and failover.

6\. Domain design
=================

6.1 Stock ledger and availability
---------------------------------

*   inv.stock\_ledger is insert-only (grants plus a trigger rejecting update and delete), partitioned by month. Quantity is signed; rows carry item, location, lot, optional serial or unit, movement type, unit cost, reference and reason.
*   **On hand** = latest month-end snapshot + ledger rows since. **Available** = on hand − active reservations. Both are views; no mutable counters.
*   **Cost:** moving average per item, updated on receipt and on landed-cost posting, recorded in an append-only cost history. Finished-unit cost is the sum of component cost snapshots plus labour at a configured rate per routing minute.

6.2 Landed cost
---------------

1.  Every charge on a shipment is converted to GH₵ at its own recorded rate and flagged recoverable or not (recoverable tax is excluded from cost).
2.  Each charge has an allocation basis: value, weight, volume, quantity or manual. Lines on the shipment’s GRNs form the basis set.
3.  Shares are computed per line and rounded by the largest-remainder method so allocations sum exactly to the charge.
4.  Unit landed cost = (line goods value in GH₵ + allocated charges) ÷ accepted quantity.
5.  Posting writes allocations, updates lot cost, appends cost history and queues GL entries. A run can be reversed and re-run; reversal needs approval after the period closes.
6.  **Late charges:** if a charge arrives after some stock has been issued, the part belonging to remaining stock adjusts the average; the part belonging to issued stock posts to a landed-cost variance account.

### Worked example (illustrative figures)

| **Item** | **Qty** | **Goods value (GH₵)** | **Freight 8,400 (value)** | **Duty 6,300 (value)** | **Clearing 1,500 (qty)** | **Landed total** | **Per unit** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SSD 512 GB | 100 | 48,000 | 4,800 | 3,600 | 1,000 | 57,400 | 574.00 |
| RAM kit | 50 | 36,000 | 3,600 | 2,700 | 500 | 42,800 | 856.00 |
| **Total** | 150 | 84,000 | 8,400 | 6,300 | 1,500 | 100,200 |  |

Goods are USD 7,000 at an illustrative rate of 12.00. SSD receives 4,000/7,000 of value-based charges.

6.3 Currency and tax
--------------------

*   Money is bigint minor units with a currency code; GH₵ is the base currency. Foreign-currency documents store the rate used; payments store their own rate, and realised difference is posted on settlement.
*   Rates come from core.exchange\_rates with a named source and effective date; a manual override needs approval and is audited.
*   Tax is computed per line from core.tax\_rates effective on the document date and stored on the line. Nothing is hard-coded.
*   Rounding is half-up per line; totals are sums of lines so documents always add up.

6.4 Unit state machine
----------------------

| **From** | **Event** | **To** | **Guard** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| planned | material issued | building | Components issued; serials captured |
| building | all mandatory steps done | testing | Checklist complete |
| testing | required tests passed | qc\_hold | All required test types passed |
| qc\_hold | QC pass | in\_stock | Inspector ≠ builder; final serial assigned; cost snapshot written |
| qc\_hold | QC fail | rework | Defect code recorded; rework order opened |
| rework | retest requested | testing | Rework closed with a note |
| in\_stock | reserved by order | reserved | Partial unique index: one active reservation per unit |
| reserved | dispatched | dispatched | Dispatch note posted; warranty record created on handover |
| dispatched | claim opened | in\_service | Service ticket open |
| in\_service | repair closed | dispatched | Genealogy updated with replaced parts |
| any not dispatched | scrap approved | scrapped | Approval recorded; e-waste entry |
| dispatched | return approved | in\_stock or quarantine | Condition check outcome |

6.5 Concurrency and integrity
-----------------------------

*   Serial allocation: SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on candidate units plus a partial unique index on active reservations.
*   Money and stock functions run at SERIALIZABLE with bounded retry.
*   Optimistic concurrency: rows carry version; clients send If-Match.
*   Document numbers are gap-free per series through core.next\_doc\_no(series) with a row-locked counter.
*   Closed fiscal periods are enforced by trigger on fin.journal\_entries.

6.6 Accounting postings
-----------------------

| **Event** | **Debit** | **Credit** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Goods receipt | Inventory – components | Goods received not invoiced |
| Landed cost posted | Inventory – components | Accrued import charges |
| Supplier invoice matched | Goods received not invoiced; input VAT | Accounts payable |
| Unit finalised | Inventory – finished goods | Inventory – components; labour absorbed |
| Dispatch and invoice | Accounts receivable | Internal sales revenue; output VAT |
| Cost of sales | Cost of goods sold | Inventory – finished goods |
| Payment received / made | Bank or cash / Accounts payable | Accounts receivable / Bank or cash |
| Adjustment, scrap | Inventory loss | Inventory |
| Covered repair | Warranty expense | Inventory (parts); labour absorbed |

Postings are generated by the worker from outbox events, idempotent per source document and event, and blocked in closed periods.

SA Super Admin · MG Management · PI Procurement & Imports · IS Inventory & Sales · FS Finance & Service · AT Assembly Technician · QI QC Inspector. ● full ◐ limited (own or assigned records, within a limit, read-only subset, or approval step) – none.  
The Super Admin deliberately has no business write or approval rights; administering the system and operating the business are separate duties. Break-glass use is logged and alerts Management.

### Segregation of duties enforced in code

*   A requester cannot approve their own PO, adjustment, discount, expense or refund.
*   The QC Inspector of a unit cannot be its builder.
*   Supplier bank detail changes: requested by Procurement, verified by Finance, approved by Management.
*   Landed-cost reversal after a period closes needs Management approval.
*   Only the Super Admin edits users and scopes; every change is audited and emailed to Management.

8\. Threat model
================

Method: STRIDE across the boundaries (browser, edge, API, database, third parties) plus abuse cases for an internal procurement, stores and finance environment. Assets: money and valuation, stock and serial integrity, supplier data, staff and contact data, licence keys, audit evidence.

| **#** | **Threat** | **Vector** | **Controls** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | Account takeover | Phished or reused password | Mandatory TOTP, short sessions, login alerts, lockout, optional SSO and Cloudflare Access |
| T2 | Privilege escalation | Tampering with role or scope claims | Only the Super Admin edits scopes; JWT claims from hook; RLS and functions re-check; changes audited and emailed |
| T3 | Fictitious supplier or changed bank details | Insider or email fraud | Dual control for bank changes, call-back verification step, supplier status workflow, alerts on new supplier plus first payment |
| T4 | Approval evasion | Splitting POs below limits | Aggregated rule per supplier and period, flagged patterns report |
| T5 | Inventory shrinkage | Silent adjustments or unrecorded issues | Insert-only ledger, approved adjustments, cycle counts, variance dashboards |
| T6 | Landed cost manipulation | Biased allocation or hidden charges | Allocation method recorded per charge, reversal approval, estimate versus actual variance report |
| T7 | Exchange-rate manipulation | Favourable manual rate | Named source per rate, manual override approval, audit, variance alerts |
| T8 | Genealogy tampering | Editing component links to hide a defect | Append-only genealogy; replacements are new rows linked to a ticket; edits audited |
| T9 | QC bypass | Technician passes own work | Database constraint on inspector ≠ builder; override only by Management with reason |
| T10 | Price or discount tampering | Modified request | Server computes prices; snapshots; margin guardrail; approvals above limit |
| T11 | IDOR and over-broad reads | Guessing IDs or requesting other users’ data | RLS ownership and scope checks, unguessable UUIDs, authorisation tests, technicians see assigned units only |
| T12 | Licence-key exposure | Over-broad read or log leak | Encrypted at rest, licence.view scope, access logged, never in logs or exports |
| T13 | Bulk data exfiltration | Export abuse | Export scope, row limits, audit, alerts on unusual volume, watermarked files |
| T14 | Malicious upload | Infected customs document or photo | Type and size allow-list, antivirus scan job, no execution, private bucket, signed short-lived URLs |
| T15 | Injection and XSS | Untrusted input | Parameterised queries, Zod validation, output encoding, strict CSP, Semgrep rules |
| T16 | Supply-chain compromise | Malicious dependency or leaked CI secret | Lockfiles, Renovate, provenance, least-privilege CI tokens, gitleaks |
| T17 | Audit tampering | Edit or delete audit rows | Insert-only grants, trigger rejects update and delete, periodic hash checkpoint stored in R2 |
| T18 | Denial of service | Flood | Cloudflare protection, API rate limits, queue back-pressure |
| T19 | Data loss or ransomware | Operator error or vendor incident | PITR, nightly encrypted dumps to a second provider, restore drills, least-privilege DB roles |
| T20 | Email spoofing and phishing | Fake system notifications | SPF, DKIM, DMARC; emails contain no login or token links, only deep links requiring sign-in |
| T21 | Future API-client abuse | Leaked service credential | Hashed secrets, narrow scopes, rotation, IP allow-list, per-client rate limits, disabled by default |
| T22 | Stale access | Leavers or role changes | Leaver checklist, same-day suspension, quarterly access review, inactivity auto-suspend |

### Control checklist

*   HSTS, secure cookies, SameSite=Lax, CSRF protection, strict CSP and frame-ancestors.
*   Service-role keys only on the server; the browser uses the anon key and RLS.
*   Per-environment secrets; production access limited to named admins with MFA.
*   Pre-launch penetration test against OWASP ASVS level 2 targets and a signed-off restore drill.

9\. API specification
=====================

9.1 Conventions
---------------

| **Topic** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| Base and versioning | https://api.<domain>/v1; breaking changes create /v2; OpenAPI 3.1 generated from Zod; typed client in packages/types |
| Auth | Authorization: Bearer <JWT> for staff; API clients use client credentials with their own scopes; scopes read from claims |
| Idempotency | Idempotency-Key required on POSTs that post to ledgers, create documents or move money; replay returns the original response |
| Concurrency | Rows carry version; PATCH and PUT require If-Match; mismatch returns 412 |
| Pagination and filters | Cursor-based ?limit=50&cursor=…; filter\[field\]=value; whitelisted sort fields; max 200 |
| Errors | RFC 9457 problem+json with code, detail, field errors and trace\_id |
| Money and time | Integer minor units in \_minor fields with currency; ISO 8601 UTC; clients show Africa/Accra |
| Rate limits | 600/min per user; heavy endpoints (reports, exports) stricter; 429 with Retry-After |
| Webhooks | Outbound events from the outbox for future integrations; HMAC-signed; inbound webhooks (future payments) verified on the raw body before parsing |

9.2 Endpoints
-------------

### Identity, admin and approvals

| **Method and path** | **Scope** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET, PATCH /me | any | Own profile and notification preferences |
| GET, POST /users · PATCH /users/{id} | users.manage | Invite, update, suspend |
| GET /roles · PATCH /users/{id}/scopes | roles.manage | Role templates and per-user scopes |
| GET /audit-log | audit.read | Search audit trail |

9.3 Representative contracts
----------------------------

### POST /v1/goods-receipts/{id}/post

Headers: Authorization, Idempotency-Key: 6f1c…  
→ 200 { "grn\_no": "GRN-2026-000145", "status": "posted",  
"ledger\_rows": 14, "quarantined": \[ { "item\_id": "…", "qty": 2 } \] }  
→ 409 problem+json code="GRN\_ALREADY\_POSTED"  
→ 422 problem+json code="SERIAL\_REQUIRED" detail="Item CPU-I5-13400 requires serials"

### POST /v1/shipments/{id}/landed-cost/run

{ "charge\_ids": \["…","…"\], "dry\_run": false }  
→ 201 { "run\_no": "LC-2026-000031", "total\_allocated\_ghs\_minor": 1470000,  
"lines": \[ { "grn\_line\_id": "…", "item": "SSD-512", "added\_minor": 940000,  
"new\_unit\_cost\_minor": 57400 } \] }  
→ 409 code="PERIOD\_CLOSED" | 422 code="NO\_ACCEPTED\_LINES"

### POST /v1/units/{id}/qc

{ "result": "pass", "checklist": { "keyboard": true, "display": true },  
"defects": \[\], "notes": "" }  
→ 201 { "inspection\_no": "QC-2026-000402", "unit\_serial": "UPSA-LAP-2026-000184" }  
→ 403 code="INSPECTOR\_BUILT\_UNIT"

### Error body

{ "type": "https://docs.<domain>/errors/unit-unavailable", "title": "Unit unavailable",  
"status": 409, "code": "UNIT\_UNAVAILABLE", "detail": "Serial … is reserved.",  
"trace\_id": "4bf92f3577b34da6" }

10\. Performance and scalability
================================

| **Surface** | **Budget** | **How** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lists | ≤ 2 s first page at 50k rows | Cursor pagination, composite and partial indexes, column-selective queries, virtualised tables |
| Document saves and postings | p95 ≤ 800 ms | Single transactional function per posting; pooled connections |
| Dashboards | ≤ 2 s | Materialised views refreshed on schedule and by event; read replica if needed |
| Reports and exports | 100k rows ≤ 30 s | Background job, streamed file to storage, signed link by email |
| API reads | p95 ≤ 300 ms | No N+1 (query review in CI), compression, HTTP/2 |
| Search | Suggestions ≤ 200 ms | Trigram and prefix indexes, debounced input |

*   Index every foreign key and every list filter; partial indexes for active rows; BRIN on time-ordered ledger partitions.
*   Monthly partitions for ledger, audit and notifications; pg\_cron creates partitions, snapshots and refreshes views.
*   Transaction-pooled connections for the API; direct connections for migrations and pg-boss; statement and lock timeouts.
*   EXPLAIN budgets in CI for the 20 key queries against a dataset ten times the expected volume.
*   k6 scenarios before go-live: 15 concurrent staff on mixed workload, a 100k-row export, a 500-line GRN post, and a landed-cost run across 200 lines.

11\. Observability and operations
=================================

*   Structured logs with trace\_id, user id and entity ids; no personal data or secrets.
*   OpenTelemetry traces and metrics to Grafana Cloud; Sentry for frontend and backend errors with release tracking.
*   Business alerts: failed GL postings, stuck jobs, shipments past ETA, approvals waiting beyond SLA, ledger invariant checks, backup freshness.
*   Better Stack uptime checks and a status page for UPSA IT.
*   One-page runbooks: outage, data restore, stuck jobs, leaver, suspected account compromise.
*   PITR for 7 days; nightly encrypted dump to R2 kept 35 days plus monthly archive; quarterly restore rehearsal.

12\. Engineering practices
==========================

*   Trunk-based development; every PR gets a Vercel preview and a Supabase branch database.
*   CI gates: types, lint, unit and pgTAP tests, Playwright smoke, axe, CodeQL, Semgrep, gitleaks, dependency review, bundle budget.
*   Forward-only SQL migrations using expand/contract; destructive changes need a second reviewer.
*   Feature flags for risky releases; production deploys on weekday mornings with a rollback plan.
*   Definition of done includes tests for scopes, audit entries and idempotency for any mutating endpoint.

14\. Decisions to confirm
=========================

1.  Hosting region after the latency test, and whether UPSA requires local hosting.
2.  Who operates production and who owns the cloud accounts (UPSA as organisation owner with Codey Dev as delegated admin is recommended).
3.  Single sign-on through UPSA’s Google or Microsoft tenant.
4.  Retention periods for audit, shipment documents and financial records.
5.  Exchange-rate source and the default allocation basis for each charge type.
6.  Hardware: tablets at the bench, scanners and label printers.
